subject: Streaming chat: sudden tail-latency & error-rate increase during peak window
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@polarishealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez, marissa_cole
Cc: support@polarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 21:10:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Sergio / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in user experience across our virtual care chat between 19:30-21:00 PT tonight. KPIs: p95 response latency is up ~2.5x and p99 is spiking intermittently to >8s. Clients report reconnects and partial message duplication in the chat UI (SSE-backed).

We attached a few log snippets and a PNG showing the error-rate jump. This is happening only during peak appointment load — same pattern we saw in June but worse. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (hosted API streaming path) or something on our integration? We’re live with a big partner tomorrow and this is blocking go/no-go.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Lead Integrations, Polaris Health
attachments: polaris_peak-20260921-logs.txt, sse-error-snapshot-20260921.png
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel, rachel_kim, marissa_cole
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@polarishealth.com>, support@polarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 21:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Looping dev & infra. Key context: customer sees p95~2.5x and p99 >8s during 19:30-21:00 PT. They use SSE streaming endpoint (hosted), moderate concurrency per connection (avg seq len ~180 tokens).

Ask: can infra confirm whether we had any autoscaling events, queue buildup, or kernel fallback for quantized endpoints in that window? Rachel, can you prioritize a perf trace and compare kernel selection & KV cache hit rates? Dev, please check routing, batching, and any queued request growth. I’ll keep Alex notified.

— Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez, rachel_kim
Cc: marissa_cole
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 22:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Quick update from infra triage: we see a pattern of sustained micro-bursts in request concurrency to the hosted streaming fleet in us-west1 between 19:28-20:55 PT. Autoscaling executed but there was a short time (approx 45s) when tail-latency amplification occurred due to a mismatched batching heuristic on older runtime hosts (pre-quant-opt). That caused some requests to be routed to fallback kernels with higher per-token latency. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% for these traces (probable cold-shard churn).

I’ve captured a flamegraph and a kernel-selection trace and linked them to INF-9876. No evidence of customer mis-integration yet. Root cause hypothesis: concurrent cold-starts + mis-sized batching window under bursty arrival -> intermittent p99 regressions.

Will push a hotfix to adjust batching thresholds and pin routing away from pre-quant-opt hosts for now. ETA for hotfix deploy: 90 minutes. I’ll open a rollback if we see regressions.

— Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineer
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@polarishealth.com>, sergio_alvarez, dev_patel, rachel_kim
Cc: support@polarishealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 00:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Alex — thanks for the logs. We see the same jump in our observability (token-level latency stair-step and error-rate bump on SSE connections). Immediate mitigations in flight: 1) temporarily disable batch window expansion for streaming endpoints in us-west1, 2) route critical customer traffic to a newer host pool with quant-opt kernels, 3) enable aggressive KV cache population for Polaris session keys.

I’ll coordinate a canary for the hotfix at 02:00 PT and will send a brief post-mortem once we’ve validated. Can you confirm whether Polaris will keep peak load steady for a 10-minute canary window (we’ll throttle if needed)?

— Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@polarishealth.com>
To: marissa_cole, sergio_alvarez
Cc: dev_patel, support@polarishealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 01:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Marissa / Sergio,

We can hold steady — Polaris can run a controlled peak from 02:00-02:12 PT on our staging traffic mirror (no patient data). Please run the canary then; we need confirmatory numbers before our partner launch. Please also share the Sentry/trace link when available — I’ll forward to our SREs.

Appreciate the quick triage.
Alex
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@polarishealth.com>, marissa_cole, dev_patel, rachel_kim, grace_oconnor
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime chat degraded — spikes in p95/p99 this evening

Follow-up: Hotfix deployed and canary executed at 02:00 PT. Short summary: p95 dropped back to baseline and p99 tail occurrences reduced by ~70% during the canary. We still see small jitter when cold-shard rebalances happen; long-term fix will be a KV cache pre-warm and a batching heuristic update across the fleet (INF-9876).

Action items:
- Dev to schedule full rollout and monitor INF-9876 (Dev).
- Product to include an optional customer config to pin routing to quant-opt hosts (Marissa + Rachel).
- CS to communicate ETA for full rollout and any temporary mitigations to Polaris (Sergio).

Alex — we’ve shared the trace + flamegraph in the ticket and the drive folder above. Expect a detailed post-mortem by EOD. I’ll also propose a short SLA credit for the incident per our enterprise playbook; please let me know if you’d like to pursue that.

— Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
